gap: No result ChatGPT got states Mobile Pixels' own three-step cable order for the Duex Plus DS (USB-C alone; then add HDMI; then HDMI plus the USB-C cable on the USB-A adapter), which is what lets it run on a 13-inch laptop whose USB-C port carries no video.
standout_why: Compared against the three cited pages (thedadsneeze.com, itechguides.com, wondrik.com) and the mobilepixels.us blog result. thedadsneeze already has most of this angle: Duex Plus DS at 13-14.5 inch and 1.3 lb, 'USB-C or mini HDMI', and Apple's limits (M1/M2 Air one screen, M3 two only with the lid closed). wondrik has the base M1/M2 one-display limit but nothing on M3. itechguides only says 'many 13- to 14-inch laptops' and to check the lid. What they lack is the maker's cable order, including the USB-A power path, Apple's exact M3 conditions, and Apple's statement that the M4 and M5 Air drive two screens with the lid open. The Trio 3 Pro driver need on base M1/M2 is on the Mobile Pixels blog, which ChatGPT got but did not cite.
decides: It confirms the pick rather than changing it. The Duex Plus DS adds one screen, which is exactly what a base M1-M3 MacBook Air 13 drives with the lid open, so it needs no driver there, and Mobile Pixels documents an HDMI fallback for laptops without USB-C video. Two-screen rows (FOPO S7, Trio 3 Pro) need a caveat on a 13-inch Air: both screens run natively only on M4/M5, and Apple's M3 two-display mode needs the lid closed, which an extender hung on the open lid cannot use. I could not open Mobile Pixels' or FOPO's product pages today (HTTP 429), so the Duex Plus DS's 13-inch fit range and the FOPO S7's 12-inch start must be re-read from the makers before the page states them.

findings.label: Maker's connection order (video path)
findings.value: 1) USB-C to C cable alone if the laptop has a USB-C port; 2) if that does not work, also connect the HDMI cable; 3) if neither works, USB-C to C cable with the USB-A adapter plus the HDMI cable
findings.source_title: Mobile Pixels Duex Plus DS installation page
findings.note: Maker's wording: 'If your laptop has USB-C port, please directly connect the monitor by using the USB-C to C cable'; 'If your laptop does not work with USB-C to C cable, please also connect the HDMI cable'; 'If it does not work with the first two methods, please connect USB-C to C cable with USB-A adapter and HDMI cable.' No driver is mentioned on the page. The page does not use the term DisplayPort Alt Mode.

findings.label: Mounting method
findings.value: Magnetic plates with adhesive stickers on the back of the laptop lid; unit centered on the back of the laptop
findings.source_title: Mobile Pixels Duex Plus DS installation page
findings.note: 'Place the magnetic plates towards the monitor side and remove the adhesive stickers'; 'Make sure that Duex Plus DS is centered in the back the laptop.' The page gives no laptop-size range and no lid exclusions.

findings.label: MacBook Air 13-inch (M2, 2022): external displays and USB-C video
findings.value: One external display (up to 6K at 60 Hz) alongside the built-in display; 'Native DisplayPort output over USB-C'
findings.source_title: MacBook Air (M2, 2022) - Tech Specs - Apple Support
findings.note: Apple's spec. One added screen uses the whole allowance, so a single-screen extender runs natively and a two-screen extender cannot light both without a display driver.

findings.label: MacBook Air M3: conditions for two external displays
findings.value: Two external displays only with the lid closed, on power, with an external keyboard and mouse or trackpad, on macOS Sonoma 14.3 or later; with the lid open the second external display 'will go dark or disconnect'
findings.source_title: Use dual monitors with your MacBook Air and MacBook Pro with M3 chip - Apple Support (published 2024-07-30)
findings.note: Inference, not Apple's words: an attached extender hangs on the open lid, so an M3 Air drives one of its screens natively.

findings.label: MacBook Air M4 and M5: external displays
findings.value: Up to two external displays simultaneously in addition to the built-in display (two up to 6K at 60 Hz); closing the lid does not raise the count
findings.source_title: How many displays can be connected to MacBook Air - Apple Support (published 2026-03-10)
findings.note: This is the Apple basis for 'both screens of a two-screen extender light natively only on an M4 or M5 Air'. It needs one video-capable USB-C port per screen; the Air has two.

findings.label: Maker's fit range and Mac driver need (maker's blog)
findings.value: 'adds two 14.1-inch 2240 x 1400 IPS displays to a 13- to 16-inch laptop'; base M1 and M2 MacBooks 'need Mobile Pixels' free driver to run both screens'; M-series Pro and Max chips and all M4 and M5 Macs do not; 4.13 lb
findings.source_title: What's the Best Portable Monitor Under $500? | Mobile Pixels
findings.note: The maker's blog says 13-16 inch, while Dealectric's record of the product page (read 2026-11-21) says 15-16 inch. I could not open the product page today to settle it, so say whose figure it is. The blog makes no M3 statement. Its dated Trio price ($433.49 on Oct 22, 2026) is not today's price.

findings.label: What the cited rival already states (not maker-verified today)
findings.value: Fit 13-14.5 inch laptops, 1.3 lb, USB-C or mini HDMI with both cables included, magnetic plates on the lid; it lists the Duex Max DS at 14-17 inch
findings.source_title: Best Laptop Screen Extender (2026): 7 Picks From $90
findings.note: These are the rival's figures, used for the standout comparison only. The same page says M1/M2 Airs support one external screen and M3 Airs two only with the lid closed. It gives no lid dimensions and no USB-A power path.

findings.label: What the other cited rivals state on compatibility
findings.value: wondrik: 'a base M1 or M2 MacBook Air drives a single external display' and every Mac USB-C/Thunderbolt port since 2015 carries DisplayPort video, with nothing on M3. itechguides: Duex Plus DS 'for many 13- to 14-inch laptops', 'Confirm the laptop's lid dimensions and mounting method', with no Mac display limit for it
findings.source_title: Which Portable Monitor Should You Buy? | Wondrik
findings.note: The itechguides quotes come from https://www.itechguides.com/15-best-laptop-screen-extenders-for-2026-boost-your-productivity/ (read 2026-11-26; the last 3,518 characters of that page were not read).
